components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for backward
            compatibility; when the structured fields are supplied it is derived
            from them. On output it is the composed address: the normalized
            'addressLine1', with a single space and the normalized 'addressLine2'
            appended when 'addressLine2' is present.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. When
            supplied it is preferred over the flat 'address'. An owner is valid
            when it supplies an address in either form: a non-blank
            'addressLine1', or the flat 'address'.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal
            address (e.g. unit or suite). When present it is normalized and
            appended to the composed 'address' after a single space.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped;
            a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped
            from the national digits. The stored value must have 8 to 15 digits
            after the '+' (e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'george.franklin@example.com'
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be
            valid for the owner's city per a fixed table keyed by the city's region
            ('Sydney' -> NSW 2000-2099, 'Melbourne' -> VIC 3000-3099, 'Brisbane' ->
            QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
            A postcode that is malformed or out of range for the city's region is
            rejected with a 400. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-

    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            selfLink:
              title: Self link
              description: >-
                The canonical relative URL of this owner, formed as '/api/owners/'
                followed by the owner's id.
              type: string
              example: '/api/owners/1'
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            salutation:
              title: Salutation
              description: >-
                The owner's salutation, composed as the honorific 'title' and the
                'lastName' separated by a single space when a title is present, or
                just the 'lastName' when no title is given.
              type: string
              example: 'DR Franklin'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The stored E.164 'telephone' formatted for humans: the country code, a
                single space, then the national digits grouped in threes (e.g. the stored
                '+61412345678' is presented as '+61 412 345 678'). The raw 'telephone'
                field keeps its canonical E.164 form.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region), derived by preferring the postcode: a 4-digit
                postcode within a known region's range ('NSW' 2000-2099, 'VIC' 3000-3099,
                'QLD' 4000-4099) yields that region. When the postcode is absent or in no known
                range, it falls back to a fixed city-to-region table ('Sydney' -> 'NSW',
                'Melbourne' -> 'VIC', 'Brisbane' -> 'QLD'). A city not in the table with no
                region-bearing postcode derives the locality 'UNKNOWN'.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The owner's IANA timezone name, derived from the locality (region) via a fixed
                region-to-timezone table ('NSW' -> 'Australia/Sydney', 'VIC' -> 'Australia/Melbourne',
                'QLD' -> 'Australia/Brisbane'). A region not in the table derives no timezone.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            memberId:
              title: Member ID
              description: >-
                The owner's unified member id, formatted '<REGION><FY><HASH8><CHK>'. REGION is the
                region derived from the owner's postcode ('NSW', 'VIC', 'QLD', or 'UNKNOWN'). FY is
                the two-digit fiscal year the owner's business-day-adjusted registrationDate falls
                in (see 'fiscalYear'). HASH8 is the first eight upper-case hex characters of the
                SHA-256 digest of the owner's normalized telephone concatenated with the last name.
                CHK is a single Luhn check digit computed over the digits of '<REGION><FY><HASH8>'.
                On a collision with an existing owner's member id, '-<n>' is appended with the
                smallest n of 2 or more that makes it unique.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW271A2B3C4D5'
              readOnly: true
            fiscalYear:
              title: Fiscal year
              description: >-
                The fiscal year the owner's business-day-adjusted registrationDate falls in,
                formatted 'FY<YY>', taken from the FY component of the owner's memberId. The fiscal
                year starts on 1 July and is named for the calendar year in which it ends, so a
                registrationDate on or after 1 July belongs to the next calendar year's fiscal year;
                YY is the last two digits of that year.
              type: string
              example: 'FY27'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by every owner in the same household - those with
                the same last name (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) and
                postcode. It is the first 12 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the normalized
                last name and postcode joined with '|', so owners with the same last name and
                postcode derive it automatically. A second owner in the same household is
                rejected as a duplicate unless it opts in with 'sharesHousehold'.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4e5f6'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived duplicate-detection key, formed by joining the normalized
                telephone, the email (or an empty string when absent) and the householdId with
                '|' separators (normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId). A create
                is rejected as a duplicate only when this whole key equals that of an existing
                owner.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|a1b2c3d4e5f6'
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners, at the time this owner was created, sharing the
                same first name and last name, compared case-insensitively.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points, computed on creation. Starts at 0;
                add 2 when an email is present; add 1 when namesakeCount is 0; add 2 for
                a household of 3 or more; add 3 when at least one fiscal year has elapsed
                since registrationDate (measured from registrationDate to today, counting
                1-July boundaries crossed).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's numeric membership level, derived from membershipPoints:
                1 (0-1 points), 2 (2-3 points), 3 (4-5 points), 4 (6 or more points).
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            ownerSegment:
              title: Owner segment
              description: >-
                The owner's segment, formatted '<TIER>_<AREA>'. TIER is 'PREMIUM' when
                membershipLevel is 3 or more, otherwise 'STANDARD'. AREA is 'METRO' when the
                locality is a known region ('NSW', 'VIC' or 'QLD'), otherwise 'REGIONAL'.
              type: string
              enum:
                - PREMIUM_METRO
                - PREMIUM_REGIONAL
                - STANDARD_METRO
                - STANDARD_REGIONAL
              example: 'STANDARD_METRO'
              readOnly: true

                registration date at the time this owner was created, otherwise false.

              type: boolean

              readOnly: true

              enum:

              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true

                owner's 'registrationDate': 'MINOR' when under 18, 'ADULT' from 18 to

              enum:

                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true

              example: false
              readOnly: true

              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true

              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true

              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:

I implemented the `riskFlag` field on the owner read model so it returns `true` when any of the three conditions hold, `false` otherwise.

**Changes:**

It ORs the three signals, reusing the already-computed `possibleDuplicate` flag, the `capacityWarning` flag (which is exactly "city over its soft capacity" — 40+ owners), and the new disposable-adjacent email check. All three underlying flags are treated null-safely (legacy/seed owners → not set), and the result is always a non-null boolean.

The one existing test (`coreRiskFlagFalseNormally`) — a unique, email-less owner in an empty city — correctly yields `riskFlag = false`.
